invariants: TIME-01: Time the full user operation through its reported result, including integrity checks, policy metadata, required barriers and receipt commitment where applicable.
TIME-02: Count only trials whose outcome matches the independent byte, metadata and state oracle for their workload.
TIME-03: Label cache class, source-consistency, verification, durability and storage topology. Match assurance and resource profiles before drawing regression or relative-throughput conclusions.
TIME-04: Keep failures and timeouts with results. A run missing required evidence cannot pass a performance gate.

budgets.enforcement: Review thresholds apply to repeated measurements with identical assurance, hardware, build and cache class. GUI/control values are design targets pending native measurements. Correctness and preservation gates precede performance review.

baseline.workload: Separate pairs of 4 KiB and 64 MiB regular files, including equal, byte-zero mismatch and last-byte mismatch. Sequential access to generated extents under a warm host page cache.

4 KiB and 64 MiB synthetic inputs, each copied into a fresh target with a preprovisioned profile on one ext4 guest volume. Include publication and receipt reporting, then independently check final bytes, required fixture metadata and committed-state inspection.

future.fixture: Deterministic 1M and 5M entries, deep and broad trees, 0–4 KiB files plus 64 MiB–4 GiB mixed extents, case-fold collision and unreadable subtree controls.
future.prerequisite: Complete bounded tree inventory and diff, including explicit unsupported-entry accounting.
metrics: verified files and bytes per second

future.fixture: Start with sequential 1 GiB and 4 GiB fixtures and fixed-seed 4 KiB random-position reads and range rewrites. Use physical HDD, SATA SSD, NVMe, separate disks and isolated network storage. Include sparse and incompressible variants, then measure warm and dedicated cold-cache classes.
future.prerequisite: Provision and identify physical topology, filesystem, mount and cache behavior. A guest ext4 volume supplies functional coverage only for this matrix.

future.fixture: 64 MiB and 1 GiB verified transfers over isolated LAN and shaped WAN. Start at 1/40/150 ms RTT, 0/0.5/2% seeded loss and 20/100/1000 Mbit/s. Include disconnect and bad retained-range controls.
future.prerequisite: Qualified SSH/SFTP endpoints and capability, identity, readback and recovery evidence.

future.fixture: Run a common verified transfer over kernel WireGuard and embedded WireGuard with the same peer and measured route. Vary MTU, RTT, loss and tunnel reconnection under load.
future.prerequisite: Embedded-to-kernel interoperability, route-loss no-fallback and tunnel identity evidence.

future.fixture: Generated album and 1 GiB binary on authorized shared storage. Pin device, host build, USB 2/3 and modeled Wi-Fi conditions; run supported stream counts up to the tested capability bound. Include a disconnect and held-temperature repeat.
future.prerequisite: Qualified Android USB and wireless adapters, explicit per-device permissions and safe reconnect.

future.fixture: Use the same 64 MiB and 4 GiB fixtures with independently checked stable snapshots of intended bytes. Interrupt at fixed staging fractions, just before publication and after publication. Corrupt one checkpoint in each relevant profile.
future.prerequisite: Stage timing instrumentation and deterministic crash-boundary estimates. Preserve ordinary readback/barrier behavior for every timed result.

future.fixture: Pathological long/repeated lines, mostly equal large trees and millions of result rows, with user input and cancellation during backup throughput load.
future.prerequisite: Native comparison UI with phase timing and qualified bounded result virtualization.

future.fixture: First full snapshot of deterministic mixed/repeated content, strict unchanged scan, rename-only, inserted-block and rewrite snapshots; verify all retained versions by restoration.
future.prerequisite: Verified backup and restore, independent repository lineage and metadata oracle, qualified reuse of stored objects.
metrics: logical bytes divided by stored bytes
